key_insight: WC–Co–Cr coating performance depends on powder morphology and spray method: detonation spraying delivers higher hardness, while HVOF produces dense, uniform coatings with low friction.
engineering_relevance: Selecting the powder and deposition process can improve the wear resistance and durability of machine parts exposed to intensive friction and high loads.
method: Compared detonation-sprayed and HVOF-deposited WC–Co–Cr coatings.
Examined powder morphology and coating microstructure using SEM and EDS.
Evaluated coating microhardness and tribological behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports average microhardness of 1449 HV for detonation spraying and a friction coefficient of Kt = 0.143 for HVOF.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify test conditions or measurement variability, limiting direct transfer of these values to service environments.
paper_title: INVESTIGATION OF THE FORMATION OF STRUCTURE AND WEAR-RESISTANT PROPERTIES OF WC–CO–CR COATINGS PRODUCED BY HVOF AND DETONATION SPRAYING
